question: What timeline did Juniper Cloud Tools agree for their evaluation?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract any timeline, dates, deadlines, or durations that Juniper Cloud Tools agreed to for their evaluation, including decision dates, trial or pilot length, next-step meeting dates, and go-live targets, noting who proposed each and whether it was confirmed.
assumptions: The question refers to the Prospect call CALL-010 with Juniper Cloud Tools, the only catalogue entry for that company.

findings.speaker: Marcus Chen
findings.quote: We want a four-week evaluation starting immediately, with a go/no-go decision in September.
findings.context: Juniper Cloud Tools wants a four-week evaluation starting immediately, with a go/no-go decision in September. — Marcus proposed the timeline; Ava confirmed Monday start. Leo and Nina accepted it as the plan.

findings.speaker: Ava Sinclair
findings.context: The evaluation starts Monday, with Ava having blocked time for it. — Clarifying 'starting immediately'; Leo said not to spend two weeks arranging it.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: You'll have all four by Friday.
findings.context: OrbitFlow will deliver the requested technical items (three exported definitions, subflow billing answer, Postgres connector documentation) by Friday, with the definitions arriving sooner. — Nina committed to Friday; later she said the three definitions would arrive that afternoon, not Friday.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: the three definitions will be in your inbox this afternoon, not Friday.
findings.context: The three exported definitions will be in the customer's inbox the afternoon of the call rather than by Friday. — Correction of the Friday commitment by Nina.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: You'll have it in week two.
findings.context: OrbitFlow committed to a written pricing model in week two of the evaluation, at the customer's request. — Marcus asked for pricing in writing before the evaluation ends; Leo committed to week two.

findings.speaker: Marcus Chen
findings.context: Juniper's side owes the Linear backlog analysis, the Salesforce API allocation, and EU residency contract checks by Friday-equivalent next steps; Marcus and Ava split these tasks. — Leo listed the customer-side deliverables; no explicit date given for the customer items.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Four criteria. I'll write them up and send them back so we're agreed rather than remembering differently.
findings.context: Leo proposed a go/no-go-style success definition at four weeks; the customer agreed to four criteria to be written up and sent back. — Leo said he would write up the criteria so both sides are aligned; Ava proposed the fourth.

draft.answer: Juniper Cloud Tools agreed to a four-week evaluation starting Monday, with a go/no-go decision in September [C1]. Success criteria and pricing milestones were set within that window [C2][C3], and OrbitFlow's technical deliveries were due sooner [C4].

claims.text: Marcus Chen (Juniper, VP Business Operations) proposed a four-week evaluation starting immediately with a go/no-go decision in September; Leo Grant and Nina Patel of OrbitFlow accepted it as the plan.
'Starting immediately' means Monday, per Ava Sinclair (Juniper), who has blocked time for it.
Leo Grant committed to a written pricing model in week two of the evaluation, at Marcus's request.
Leo proposed a go/no-go-style success definition at four weeks; four criteria were agreed, which Leo will write up and send back.

Nina Patel committed to deliver the technical items (three exported definitions, subflow billing answer, Postgres connector documentation) by Friday, then corrected that the three definitions would arrive the afternoon of the call.

Juniper owes the Linear backlog analysis, Salesforce API allocation and EU residency contract checks as Friday-equivalent next steps, split between Marcus and Ava, but no explicit date was given for these customer items.

conflicts.topic: Delivery date for the three exported definitions
conflicts.description: Nina first committed to all items by Friday, then corrected that the three definitions would arrive the afternoon of the call, not Friday.

not_covered: No explicit date for the Juniper-side deliverables.
The exact September date for the go/no-go decision was not stated.
